children: Most global stock indexes ended the week lower. Brent crude passed $100 per barrel. Escalating U.S.–Iran geopolitical tensions sparked fears of potential oil supply disruptions and persistent inflationary pressure.

Market sentiment was further dampened as the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield climbed to its highest level since October 2023, boosting expectations for rate-hike action at the Federal Reserve’s upcoming meeting next week.
ended the week 1.6% lower amid broader concerns over macroeconomic headwinds from higher energy prices and interest rates.

The European Central Bank raised interest rates again in September, citing persistent inflationary pressures from the Middle East conflict and warning that inflation could remain elevated for an extended period.

On the data front, the Eurozone economy grew more strongly than initially estimated in the second quarter, marking its fastest quarterly expansion in years, largely driven by a sharp rebound in Ireland’s GDP.

UK GDP growth accelerated in July, beating expectations for the third straight month and suggesting the economy may be more resilient than expected in the second half of the year. UK retail sales growth slowed in August, marking the weakest pace in nearly two years.
Bank of England monetary policy meeting is due in the upcoming week, where policymakers are widely expected to keep rates on hold.

stayed strong in August, supporting expectations of further monetary tightening by the Bank of Japan. Meanwhile, economic growth in the second quarter was revised higher, helped by a smaller-than-expected decline in business investment.
